newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian stocks end slightly weaker as BHP falls.
newsitem.headline: Australian stocks end slightly weaker as BHP falls.

text.p: A further fall in heavyweight Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd shares pushed the Australian share market to a softer finish on Tuesday, ending a run of record highs.
BHP closed 53 cents lower at A$18.39 (US$14.16), following a 40 cent fall on Monday, in a market otherwise lacking momentum due to market holidays in London and New York on Monday.
"There's not much direction, we've just drifted sideways," said Richard Herring, a dealer at Burrell & Co.
The All Ordinaries Index ended down 5.9 points at 2,578.9, due almost entirely to the fall in BHP, traders said.
Gains outnumbered losses by 430 to 371 on moderate turnover of A$867 million.
Traders said the continued fall in BHP, following Monday's profit warning, spilled over to some other resource stocks, despite some earlier switching into these stocks.
CRA Ltd eased 11.5 cents to A$21.80 and WMC Ltd shed seven cents to A48.41 as the All Resources index closed down 1.04 percent on the day.
The fall in Australia's largest company BHP followed a warning of a below-expectations fourth quarter result and a flat peformance into late 1998.
Brokers said the international holidays meant there was little new overseas business, but said market sentiment remained positive following four days of record closes to Monday.
"It was a bit of a pull-back today, but generally there's still a fairly good underlying tone," said a Sydney-based dealer.
"People tonight will go looking for leads on commodity prices and markets," he said.
The retail sector kept its positive tone after strong gains on Monday, while banks also held up well.
Retailers Woolworths Ltd, Coles Myer Ltd and David Jones were all slightly firmer.

FAI Insurances topped the turnover lists again, with over 23 million shares, or 7.4 percent of the stock, going through the market. The bulk of the trade was crossed before the open. On Monday, about 20 million FAI shares were traded.
Insurer National Mutual Holdings Ltd ended unchanged after announcing interim net profit to March 31 of A$175.5 million.
